content:
- Model consistently overestimates prices in the early part of the forecast horizon, especially after sharp spikes or high historical values.
- Underestimates prices during prolonged downward trends or when true values dip below 35–40.
- Shows persistent lag in adjusting to true price drops; forecasts remain elevated longer than actuals.
- Overshoots after short-term spikes, then fails to correct downward quickly — model holds high values too long.
- Mean reversion is underappreciated: model fails to recognize that prices often return to mid-range after extreme highs or lows.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts tend to be overly optimistic in the first 5–10 days, then gradually converge — but often too late.
- When true values are clustered below 35, model fails to reduce forecast significantly, leading to persistent overestimation.
- Model exhibits “sticky” behavior — resistant to downward corrections even when true values are clearly falling.
